author: Vox
description:
We were told that airing our personal trauma in public would set us free. Instead, we got “the trauma script,” celebrity branding, and performative empathy.

Subscribe to our channel! http://goo.gl/0bsAjO

In today's episode, guest host Christine Emba talks with cultural theorist and professor Catherine Liu, author of "Traumatized: The New Politics of Public Suffering." In this scathing book, Catherine argues that our modern obsession with the "trauma script" isn't a radical act of liberation, but rather a distraction from widening economic inequality. They discuss why identity pluralism has eclipsed class struggle, how public therapy speak undermines democratic debate, and why we must move away from commodified self-absorption to focus on collective political and economic change.

01:32 Origins of the trauma script

title: The dark side of modern therapy culture | The Gray Area

author: Vox
description:
Fun fact: Bogs are incredibly good at preserving bodies, but we don’t always know why they ended up there. We do know that this started thousands of years ago and moved all the way up to occasionally the Middle Ages. So who was buried in the bogs? Were they criminals? Were they considered holy? 

Find out what other mysteries and answers can be discovered through these spongy wetlands with Anna North, the author of “Bog Queen,” on Netflix.
